newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries steady with firm tone by Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries steady with firm tone by Tokyo noon.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were mostly steady by Tokyo midday on Thursday from Wednesday's New York close, with the tone firm due to light follow-through short-covering.
Market sentiment improved as credit-tightening fears subsided slightly after employment costs index data, released on Tuesday in the United States, was lower-than-expected.

"Since the ECI, short holders have been more willing to unwind their positions, but there are still many short holders holding on to their positions," a Japanese bank trader said. "They need to see the results of unemployment data (due on Friday) to determine the trend in the long term."
The key 30-year bond firmed to 95-29/32, yielding 6.95 percent, compared with 95-26/32 in New York.
The June T-bond futures contract rose 2/32 to 109-11/32 from the previous close.

Many Japanese investors, who have refrained from buying actively, are now looking for an opportunity to buy after the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data due at 1400 GMT and unemployment data.
"It's too premature to say sentiment has turned bullish," the trader said. "Investors will need more signs about the state of the U.S. economy from payroll and NAPM data."
